description.p: A set of warm clothes
Slender shoulder pouch made from one very large acorn
A quill
When rubbed on a club or quarterstaff, the weapon becomes imbued with the Shillelah spell for 1 minute.
Inscribed upon this amulet are the words, "Greed is good" in Dwarven runes.

The Chaos Flintlock is a volatile masterpiece of dwarven ingenuity and divine mischief. A handmade firearm powered by unstable runes, holy light, and whatever spare parts Anvil had on hand, each pull of the trigger invites fate itself to meddle, unleashing anything from radiant blasts to glitter explosions, and occasionally, catastrophic brilliance. It’s less a weapon and more a gamble with the gods of invention.

This contraption has 7 charges. While holding it, you can use an action to expend 1 of its charges and choose a target within 120 feet of you. The target can be a creature, an object, or a point in space. Roll d100 and consult the following table to discover what happens.
If the effect causes you to cast a spell from the flintlock, the spell's save DC is 15. If the spell normally has a range expressed in feet, its range becomes 120 feet if it isn't already.
If an effect covers an area, you must center the spell on and include the target. If an effect has multiple possible subjects, the GM randomly determines which ones are affected.
The flintlock regains 1d6 + 1 expended charges daily at dawn. If you expend the contraption's last charge, roll a d20. On a 1, the flintlock explodes into metal shards and is destroyed.

Once per day, you can use your reaction to cast the rune. The rune glows metallic and you become incorporeal, any damage passing right through you. It is deeply unsettling, like a void is sucking you in and does not want to let you go. You take no damage from the attack but you DO take 2 psychic damage each time you use the rune.
Once per long rest your divine smite does max damage at first level (2d8 = 16) and the target has disadvantage against you on his next turn.

Once per day, on a bonus action, you can throw this small pouch of flour at a target. The pouch explodes on contact, sending flour particles airborne in a 10 foot sphere. The particles fill the air until the end of your next turn. If fire comes in contact with the sphere, it creates an explosion. Creatures in the radius take 4d6 fire damage ½ as much on DC 13 Dex save.
The bag reappears with your gear at dawn every day.
The knee pads reduce fall damage by 1d6
Once per day, using an Action, the mechanical mouse can be wound up and either set down or tossed up to 10 feet. The mouse then scampers up to 30 feet in a direction of your choosing, then detonates.
Creatures in a 10-foot radius make a DC13 Dexterity save. On a failure they take 3d8 force damage, on success, they take half damage.
The shrapnel: Any creature that fails the save is also struck by tiny fragments of tin — at the start of their next turn, they take 1d4 bleeding damage.
The reassembly: On your next turn, the mouse's scattered pieces yank themselves out of every creature still carrying shrapnel and clatter back together at your feet.
While wearing these glasses, you can read and comprehend written information in a language you understand ten times as fast.

These green and blue speckled minty sticks of chewing gum are typically found in packs containing 1d10 sticks. As an action, you can eat one stick of gum and gain the ability to imitate another creature’s voice for 1 hour. A creature that hears you can tell that the voice is an imitation by making a DC 20 Wisdom (Insight) check.

You can use an action to target one creature within 15 feet. The creature must make a DC 15 Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, the creature can’t speak a deliberate lie for 10 minutes. An affected creature is aware of the effect and can thus avoid answering questions to which it would normally respond with a lie. Such a creature can be evasive in its answers as long as the effect lasts. This property cannot be used again until the next dawn.
